title: AWS Config: resource history and compliance rules

kcs.statement: AWS Config records the configuration of your resources over time, so you can see what a resource looked like at any point in time and what changed.

AWS Config rules check resources against desired settings (for example 'S3 buckets must not be public' or 'EBS volumes must be encrypted') and flag non-compliant resources. Remediation can be automated.
AWS Config answers 'what does this resource look like, and is it compliant?' CloudTrail answers 'who made the API call that changed it?'

problem_ideas: A security group allowed port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0 last Tuesday but not today. Which service shows the change in the security group's configuration?
Compliance requires every EBS volume to be encrypted. Which feature flags unencrypted ones continuously?
Pick CloudTrail or Config: 'who opened the bucket to the public?' and 'which buckets are public right now?'
A non-compliant S3 bucket should be made private automatically. Describe the Config pieces involved.
An auditor asks what a database looked like 45 days ago. Name the service.
Explain the difference between AWS Config compliance and AWS Artifact compliance reports.
